- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); apply dampening factor to subsequent days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days below 75) after a peak, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1-2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; lag 1-2 days in sentiment-driven adjustments.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with the cycle’s midpoint; anchor forecast to 3-5 day moving average of history.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; use 10-day smoothing to avoid noise-driven spikes.
